parts.name: True (vertebrosternal) costal cartilages, ribs 1-7
parts.attachment_or_location: each rib's anterior end directly to the sternum
parts.function_note: each of ribs 1-7 has its own separate costal cartilage articulating directly with the sternum via a small synovial (ribs 2-7) or fibrocartilaginous (rib 1) joint.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

parts.name: False (vertebrochondral) costal cartilages, ribs 8-10
parts.attachment_or_location: each rib's anterior end to the cartilage of the rib above, forming the costal margin
parts.function_note: ribs 8-10 do not reach the sternum directly -- their cartilages fuse onto the cartilage above, together forming the costal margin.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

parts.name: Floating costal cartilages, ribs 11-12
parts.attachment_or_location: short cartilaginous caps on the anterior ends of ribs 11-12, ending free in the abdominal wall musculature
parts.function_note: unlike ribs 1-10, ribs 11-12 have no cartilaginous connection to the sternum or costal margin at all -- 'floating' is a structurally accurate, not just descriptive, name.
parts.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell)

function: The hyaline cartilage rods continuing each rib anteriorly, providing the rib cage the elasticity needed for breathing-related expansion/recoil that a purely bony connection to the sternum could not.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
